scope: A disposable, probe-only batch fact contributes net quantity to a stock root and positive input demand to a separate schema-owned gross-input root. Its attached ReBase validator compares the settled gross-demand range at that exact timestamp with fn::tree::before(stock_root, [effective_at]).

No production accounting schema, stock source, floor guard, compiler route, or routing document was changed. The probe extends generated adapters only inside its own in-memory database so a disposable source can use the existing temporal refresh lifecycle.

result.conclusion: Proceed to H7 implementation. The existing temporal primitives and settled validation phase can enforce gross input separately from net stock without an untracked array or a derived field reading its own local tree.
observed: Zero prior stock: one batch with input 1 and same-time output 1 rejects. Its hypothetical net delta is 0, so a net-only complete-time floor would pass; the separate gross root has demand 1 while pre-time stock is 0. The source and both roots remain unchanged.

Prior stock 10: two input facts of 6 at the same instant accept the first and reject the second because same-time aggregate gross demand is 12 against pre-time stock 10. Full source/root snapshot equality holds for the rejected second write.
The same aggregate case rejects with reversed insertion and record-ID order, with the same atomic snapshot result.
A grant at the prior timestamp supports a later input of 6. fn::tree::before at the later event remains 10; the post-event stock is 4.
Reducing or deleting that earlier grant re-runs the dependent later batch validator and rejects atomically, leaving the grant and all roots unchanged.

The gross range uses the exact half-open interval [T, T + 1ns). A valid schedule with prior stock 6, demand 6 at T, replenishment 6 at T + 0.5ms, and later demand 6 at T + 0.75ms passes with final stock 0. The probe directly observes demand 6 in [T,T+1ns) and demand 12 in [T,T+1ms), proving a millisecond upper bound would falsely combine distinct timestamps. SurrealDB preserved the one-nanosecond successor.
supported_mechanisms: Gross demand is an explicit schema-owned temporal root, not a query-time reconstructed array.
The source validator runs after `fn::rebase::refresh` has synchronized and published both memberships; the gross range includes the current source fact.

A `dependent=true` membership on stock history makes later batch facts refresh when an earlier stock contribution is edited or deleted. The probe demonstrated rejection and rollback for both operations.
The validator directly calls tree prefix/range readers. It is not a derived field and does not read its own local root through a derived dependency.
limits: This is an engine and temporal-lifecycle feasibility probe, not an H7 production schema or domain acceptance claim.
The probe fixture uses one scalar input and one scalar output per batch fact. It does not implement recipes, routing, resource/unit guards, or a generalized assembly model.

The exact timestamp interval depends on the demonstrated SurrealDB 3.2.0 nanosecond datetime resolution and exclusive upper-bound behavior; the probe does not claim behavior for other engine versions.

commands.result: passed on a local in-memory SurrealDB 3.2.0 server
